“Not me personally, however some of my family have not been so lucky.” Copper keeps a steady pace while rowing, he begins to tell a story. “As a child, my parents and I lived alone. I never thought much of it, I just enjoyed being able to play. However as I got older, I began asking questions as to why we lived alone. That was when my mother and father sat me down, and told me what the world was like.” He lets out a long sigh, “there is a group of people. Truly evil beings. They consider hunting a way to show there status. At first they hunted regular animals, but after a while that got boring. Hunting a deer is one thing, but hunting something that could potentially outsmart you? That was considered the height of skill. When dragons became harder and harder to find, someone got the bright idea. My kind were essentially dragons? Are they not? It’s basically the same thing. And so they began hunting us. They thought that by hunting my kind, it would show off there status as Hunters. These Hunters were disgusting, however they did follow at least some sort of code. They never hunted a pregnant person, nor small groups. They would be to ‘easy’. Which is why my kind is spread out. The farther we are from each other, the safer we are.”

Copper nods, “once. Many years ago, as a small one. There was a group of them. Turns out, they had been given some wrong information about my family. They believed there to be many of us, when in fact we only numbered 3. They came in the night, while we were sleeping. I awoke to sound of shattering glass. And my mother holding me. The door suddenly burst open, and they piled inside. Weapons drawn, ready for a fight. When they saw it was just me and my parents, they weren’t sorry. They were disappointed. They were expecting to have a fight, instead they saw my father pleading they spare my mother and I at least. The leader of the group was angry, this wasn’t the challenge he had hoped for, so he ordered his group to leave. However one of there members wasn’t satisfied. He wanted a trophy. So they held my father down, and removed one of his claws.” Copper looks out to the stars, “the next day, my father told me that we were lucky. That it could have been much worse.” He lets out a long sigh “From that day on, I swore I’d never let anyone I cared about get hurt again. And so i trained myself. I trained to fight, so I could protect those I love.”

How deep the Father’s love for us,
How vast beyond all measure,
That He should give His only Son
To make a wretch His treasure.
How great the pain of searing loss –
The Father turns His face away,
As wounds which mar the Chosen One
Bring many sons to glory.

Behold the man upon a cross,
My sin upon His shoulders;
Ashamed, I hear my mocking voice
Call out among the scoffers.
It was my sin that held Him there
Until it was accomplished;
His dying breath has brought me life –
I know that it is finished.

I will not boast in anything,
No gifts, no power, no wisdom;
But I will boast in Jesus Christ,
His death and resurrection.
Why should I gain from His reward?
I cannot give an answer;
But this I know with all my heart –
His wounds have paid my ransom.
